item.title: Michael Beasley Stops Delonte West In Adin Ross’ Brand Risk Ring
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Michael Beasley stopped Delonte West in the first round at Adin Ross' Brand Risk 16 after his earlier loss under MMA rules.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Beasley beat Delonte West by a first-round technical knockout at Adin Ross’ Brand Risk 16, turning a return to the streamer’s fight promotion into a better result under boxing rules.

The former NBA players met on the October 16 card at the Brand Risk Warehouse in Miami. MMA Fighting reported that West went down during the opening round and failed to beat the referee’s 10-count.

Beasley had the height and reach advantage. The report described West pressing forward with big swings, while Beasley worked from outside his range. Their exchange ended with West on the canvas and the referee stopping the contest.

The finish reversed Beasley’s experience at Brand Risk 14 in May, when he tried mixed martial arts against Lance Stephenson in Las Vegas. The pair had also competed in Big3 basketball and played one-on-one for $100,000. Stephenson took him to the mat and won with a rear-naked choke, a hold applied from behind that forced Beasley to submit.

Beasley was still open to boxing afterward, even as he made clear that grappling had given him trouble.

“Practicing getting choked and getting choked ain’t the same!” he said after that May loss.

His meeting with West brought another familiar basketball face into the ring. The two had played against each other in the NBA and China’s top league before joining Ross’ crossover event.

The bout was West’s first appearance in combat sports, while Beasley returned after the Stephenson loss. Ross’ promotion put their matchup on a card that also featured streamers, social-media personalities and R&B singer YK Osiris.

Osiris faced Deshae Frost in another boxing bout on the same show. The promotion streamed the event free across its social channels and Ross’ Kick channel, continuing its mix of established sports names and internet entertainers.

Their face-to-face meeting during fight week was friendly despite the coming contest. Interviewer Fred Beck asked West about seeing Beasley, and West described a shared past that included both competition and scuffles, Athlon Sports reported.

“Oh, yeah, yeah. We’re two fierce competitors, you know. And we both want to win. We love to win,” West said.

item.title: Treach Says Egypt Criss Knockout Drew Him Into Boxing Business
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Treach traced his boxing partnership to a call after Egypt Criss's knockout as he prepared for a November Smack fight night.
item.content:encoded:
Treach says his daughter Egypt Criss’s knockout loss led to a call that drew him into the fight business. Now he is set to appear at a Smack Fighting Championships card in November.

The Naughty By Nature rapper told the story on Drink Champs. The episode came out October 16. He said he had no role in putting together his daughter’s March fight against Jade Jones.

Treach recalled a call from promoter Damon Feldman after the bout. Feldman wanted to know how Egypt was doing. The two had known each other for years, he said. Feldman had tried to bring him into celebrity boxing before.

That call led to new talks about working together. Treach said they began with celebrity fights, then moved into the open-hand Smack format as well.

His next listed stop is Smack’s November 20 fight night at Harrah’s Philadelphia. The venue is in Chester, Pennsylvania. The event is set for 7 P.M. The poster bills him as a special guest. Justina Valentine and Chrisean Rock are the hosts.

Treach also described his dream match. He wants people to take a street dispute into the ring and leave it there.

His ties to Feldman were public well before this interview. The two appeared together on FOX 29 in May to discuss a celebrity boxing event.

Feldman spoke to AllHipHop in February about his fight plans. That interview is below.

Treach said Smack fighters can move and block shots. He described a bout with three one-minute rounds, rather than people standing still to trade slaps.

Jones knocked Egypt out in the second round in England on March 7. Treach blamed the people around his daughter, a dispute AllHipHop covered at the time.

Jones had won two Olympic gold medals. Her sport was taekwondo. That was her boxing debut. MMA Fighting reported the bout as an exhibition. It was Egypt’s first boxing bout, too.

Egypt later pushed back on the criticism. She said she made her own choices and stood by her team. The loss had not ended her plans to box.

Smack staged a fight night in September. Kimbo Slice Jr. and Crip Mac were on the card. Its TrillerTV listing paired open-hand bouts with standard boxing matches. It described one-minute Smack rounds.

The November sale page warns that the card and guest appearances can change.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Teaches Rap In 1915 Japan In “Stranger Than Heaven” Trailer
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Snoop Dogg's Orpheus puts music at the heart of a new game trailer as Makoto Daito seeks a fresh start in 1915 Japan.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg’s smuggler character turns rap coach in a new “Stranger Than Heaven” trailer set in 1915 Japan, helping a young boy find his voice.

The “Act 1: Kokura Story Trailer” arrived Friday, October 16. It shows the bond between Snoop’s character, Orpheus, and the game’s young lead, Makoto Daito, through a music lesson.

The scene links advice about turning feelings into song with a verse about being shut out and searching for a place to belong.

SEGA’s new clip follows the boy as he slips aboard Orpheus’ ship to reach Japan. His first stop is Kokura, Fukuoka. The setting opens a fictional story that runs from 1915 to 1965 across five cities.

Orpheus’ role as a mentor first came to light in May. He takes Makoto under his wing, drawing on the boy’s grasp of Japanese as they work together. He also spots Makoto’s gift for music.

Makoto, the son of an American father and a Japanese mother, grew up in the United States. After losing both parents and facing racism, he heads for his mother’s homeland. On the voyage, he meets Yu Shinjo, who becomes both his friend and rival.

Their goals soon clash. Makoto wants to survive and find a home, while Yu aims to reshape Japan. They part ways but later reunite as partners in show business.

Music also shapes what players can do. As a young singer, Makoto can gather sounds from his world and use them to create songs. Those sounds can come from trains, street life and even fights.

He can then build a show, choose the band and setlist, and shape its lights and staging. His path through Japan includes a rise in show business as well as clashes with crime groups.

Snoop’s real-life ties helped shape the cast, too. Studio head Masayoshi Yokoyama said in a June interview that Tupac Shakur’s name came up while the team and Snoop discussed who could fill another role.

Yokoyama said the studio sought approval from Tupac’s family and estate before moving ahead. Tupac’s character is named Amaru. Snoop’s son, Cordell Broadus, also has a role in the game.

The publisher says more story trailers will follow from the game’s other eras.

“Stranger Than Heaven” launches January 15, 2027, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S and PC.

item.title: D’Angelo’s Posthumous Album Comes With Unreleased Michael Jackson Collaboration
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: D’Angelo’s family unveiled ambitious archival ambitions as lrecordings and other prospective collections ar closer to public release.
item.content:encoded:
D’Angelo left behind a vault of unreleased music and his family is now preparing a posthumous album that could extend the late soul legend’s musical legacy well beyond his death.

The announcement comes from his older brother Luther Archer, who confirmed during an interview with Kiss Richmond that a new project is being assembled with six tracks identified so far. The family is also considering additional releases that could include rare recordings, B-sides and an entire collection of cover songs. 

“We’ve got an album coming out,” Archer said. “There are six tracks [so far]. But then we have a whole vault of music that’s never been released.”

Perhaps the most tantalizing revelation involves a previously unreleased recording featuring D’Angelo, Michael Jackson and Mary J. Blige. The collaboration has attracted considerable attention because it would bring together three enormously influential voices in R&B and soul.

The recording may also have a history stretching back more than a decade.

In 2014, musician Jesse Johnson publicly discussed a version of Sly and the Family Stone’s “Hot Fun in the Summertime” that reportedly featured vocals from Jackson, Blige and D’Angelo. The recording was associated with Jackson’s posthumous Xscape project but did not appear on the final album.

That earlier recording could be connected to the material Archer recently discussed, although its inclusion on the forthcoming D’Angelo album has not been confirmed. 

The potential release represents an extraordinary development for an artist whose recording career was marked by both remarkable musical achievements and lengthy periods of silence.

D’Angelo released just three studio albums during his lifetime: Brown Sugar in 1995, Voodoo in 2000 and Black Messiahin 2014.

Each project helped establish his reputation as a meticulous musician who valued artistic independence over the demands of the commercial recording industry.

His death from pancreatic cancer on Oct. 14, 2025, at age 51 brought that extraordinary career to an abrupt conclusion.

However, the existence of additional recordings suggests his musical story may have more chapters. 

Archer indicated that the family is looking beyond a single album. The possibility of separate collections of alternate recordings and covers could provide a broader examination of D’Angelo’s creative process.

Questlove previously suggested that unreleased music would eventually surface, lending additional credibility to the prospect of new recordings from the celebrated singer.

For now, no official release date, album title or complete tracklist has been announced.

item.title: Vin Rock Says He & Kay Gee Are Ready For Naughty By Nature Reunion
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Vin Rock defended his role in Naughty By Nature and said he and Kay Gee are ready to share a stage with Treach again.
item.content:encoded:
Vin Rock said he and DJ Kay Gee were ready to reunite Naughty By Nature as a three-man group.

The rapper made his position clear in an October 17 Instagram post shared with Naughty By Nature’s account. He apologized to fans who want to see the full group back in action and defended the work he has put into their career.

“Kaygee and I are ready to ROCK as the 3 Man Threat ANY GIVEN DAY!!!” he wrote.

Vin also challenged the idea that his value to the group rested only on writing verses. A commenter asked whether Treach had written his rhymes. In a reply shown in a screenshot supplied to AllHipHop, Vin answered, “Some, not all but that’s NOT the point!”

He described Naughty By Nature as a machine with many moving parts, arguing that substantial work happens before the audience sees the result. He also said Treach had been trying to go solo for 25 years.

In his caption, Vin traced their roots to New Style and East Orange, New Jersey. The post’s graphic also claimed he had been offered money to respond publicly. He did not identify who made the offers or provide a dollar figure.

Treach discussed the split on the October 16 episode of Drink Champs. In the program’s official transcript, he described his groupmates’ performances as DJ sets rather than the full group. He also claimed he wrote most of the group’s lyrics, while splitting the publishing in thirds.

Treach’s opposition to a reunion was already public. AllHipHop reported in August that Treach had ruled out a reunion during The Real Report. Vin’s latest post renewed his own willingness to perform together; it did not establish that Treach had agreed.

The group has repaired public rifts before. In a 2016 Miami New Times interview ahead of their 25th-anniversary tour, Vin described putting differences aside so the original trio could perform for fans again.

Their shared catalog includes “O.P.P.,” “Hip Hop Hooray” and “Feel Me Flow.” The Recording Academy lists Poverty’s Paradise as the group’s 1996 Best Rap Album winner.

No joint reunion date was announced in the post.

item.title: LAPD Probes Stabbings Near Taste Of Soul Festival
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Police investigated stabbings near the Crenshaw gathering, while organizers said the free music festival ended on schedule.
item.content:encoded:
Two reports of stabbings near Los Angeles’ Taste of Soul drew a police response on Saturday (October 17). The free Crenshaw festival stayed open and ended on time, its team said.

The festival’s team told ABC7 that police activity took place outside the grounds. “Police activity happened on the outskirts of the event,” they said.

The first call came in around 2:45 p.m. near Crenshaw and Martin Luther King Jr. boulevards. LAPD Officer Charles Miller told City News Service that a group had been in a fight. At least one person reportedly had a stab wound.

Those involved had left by the time police reached the scene. Police checked hospitals to try to find a victim.

LAPD’s press team later said police found two people at a hospital. They spoke with them and took assault-with-a-deadly-weapon reports over cuts. Their condition was not known.

Fire crews took one person to a hospital after a second report at 6:10 p.m., CBS LA said.

That call came from the 4200 block of Crenshaw Boulevard. ABC7 said the patient had possible stab wounds. Police had not said if the two cases had a link.

LAPD’s citywide tactical alert lasted for hours. The alert ended Saturday night.

Taste of Soul was in its 21st year. Bakewell Media and the Los Angeles Sentinel put on the event. Its hours ran from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.

The stage plan named Lucky Daye, Alex Isley, Joyce Wrice, Jenevieve and Daley on the KJLH bill. Other planned acts included Thelma Houston, Midnight Star and Switch. The three-stage plan spanned R&B, soul, gospel and Hip-Hop.

The program paired local food vendors and shops with job resources and voter sign-ups. Guests could get free health checks and help with benefits. St. John’s Community Health planned care and games for families, with five first-aid stations planned along the route.

On the site, founder Danny J. Bakewell Sr. said the goal was to support Black businesses and bring people together. The site says more than three million guests have come over 21 years.

The reports did not say what led to the stabbings.

item.title: LL Cool J Credits Bruce Lee For Doing Up To 90% Of His Own Stunts
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: LL Cool J linked his stunt work to the same personal commitment he brought to rap, while Sam Hanna faced a new chapter in New York.
item.content:encoded:
LL Cool J credited Bruce Lee with inspiring his hands-on approach to action scenes, saying he still performed most of his own stunts as Sam Hanna.

Speaking at a New York Comic Con panel for “NCIS: New York,” the 58-year-old rapper put his share at 80 to 90 percent, People reported.

“I do 80 or 90 percent of my stunts,” he said.

LL praised Lee’s drive to make screen action convincing. He also credited stunt performer Brennan Dyson, joking that some especially punishing hits called for a double.

The same commitment had shaped his work on “NCIS: Los Angeles” years earlier. In a 2011 interview, LL said doing the physical work showed his investment in Sam and gave viewers a more direct experience.

He compared handing those scenes to someone else with sending a look-alike on tour to rap in his place. Back then, he also described how learning to handle, take apart and clean weapons made him more comfortable with the role’s technical demands. He recalled sliding across a car’s trunk during a chase scene as one stunt he particularly enjoyed. At the time, LL also said he liked leaving Sam’s past a mystery.

The new series gave that familiar action hero a different kind of test. As AllHipHop previously reported, Sam’s move east followed 14 seasons on “NCIS: Los Angeles.”

The death of a friend brought Sam back to New York, showrunner Byron Balasco explained. That personal case paired him with Scott Caan’s Nick Schaeffer.

LL said Sam felt out of place after years away. The neighborhoods and people had changed, and coming back forced the character to work out where he belonged. Balasco said the series would explore the people and ties that shaped Sam before viewers met him in Los Angeles. Coming home also meant facing the responsibilities those old connections carried.

The physical side still required upkeep. LL told People before the premiere that he tried to stay consistent in the gym. He also said years of action work helped him remain calm afterward.

Asked how long he would keep playing Sam, he said he would continue while the role worked and viewers enjoyed it. CBS placed “NCIS: New York” on Tuesdays at 9 p.m. Eastern.

item.title: 50 Cent’s “Street Fighter” Tops Box Office With $31 Million Debut
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: 50 Cent brought Balrog to the big screen as “Street Fighter” pulled in an estimated $51 million worldwide in its first weekend.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent landed at the top of the box office with “Street Fighter,” which opened to an estimated $31 million in the United States and Canada.

The Paramount release took first place across 3,575 theaters, according to Sunday studio estimates reported by The Associated Press. International ticket sales added about $20 million, bringing its worldwide opening to roughly $51 million.

Box-office tracker The Numbers listed $13 million for Friday and $10.8 million for Saturday, with Sunday estimated at $7.2 million. AP said men made up 69% of the audience.

The film arrived in U.S. theaters on October 16 with 50 playing Balrog, the boxer from Capcom’s fighting games. Director Kitao Sakurai’s take put the characters in 1993, with Ryu and Ken drawn back into combat after Chun-Li recruited them for the World Warrior Tournament.

Andrew Koji played Ryu, Noah Centineo played Ken and Callina Liang played Chun-Li. The cast also included Eric André as Don Sauvage and Jason Momoa as Blanka, putting 50 in an ensemble built around the game’s fighters.

50 knew boxing years before he took the role, having practiced it from childhood through his teens. Balrog brought him back to the sport with an Australian coach. In the pre-release interviews, he also described the recovery side of the job, including massage and cryotherapy, alongside the pressure to match the character’s build.

The film reportedly cost $82 million to produce, excluding marketing and promotion. Capcom and Legendary jointly financed the adaptation as the game company pushed to bring its characters to audiences beyond gaming.

The first-place finish came with a B-minus CinemaScore, TheWrap reported, matching the grade for the 1994 “Street Fighter.” Its domestic start fell below the $38.5 million debut of “Mortal Kombat II,” another fighting-game adaptation released in May.

The weekend’s runner-up, “You Can See Everything,” brought in an estimated $15 million from 855 screens, according to AP, giving the Elizabeth Holmes documentary second place.

The new film nevertheless cleared the earlier “Street Fighter” movies’ opening weekends in unadjusted dollars. The Numbers recorded a $9.5 million debut for the 1994 film, while “Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li” opened to $4.7 million in 2009.

Final domestic figures were due Monday.

item.title: Kelly Rowland & Tina Knowles Lead birthFUND Team At Houston Walk
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Kelly Rowland and Tina Knowles will lead birthFUND’s Houston team, raising support for families seeking help with birth care.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Rowland and Tina Knowles are heading back to Houston to lead birthFUND’s team at the first Third Ward Mile, putting their hometown ties behind a maternal-care fundraiser.

The two will serve as team captains alongside birthFUND founder Elaine Welteroth at the November 28 event, People reported. Both already support the nonprofit as family funders. The new role brings them to a community walk in the neighborhood where Knowles ran Headliners, the hair salon tied to Destiny’s Child’s beginnings.

“Every mother deserves to feel safe, supported and seen when she brings life into the world,” Rowland told People. Knowles added, “Third Ward helped me raise my girls.”

birthFUND’s program helps families pay for birth care. Its need-based grants cover perinatal care and midwifery support. Birth Center Equity vets participating providers, while the Victoria Project and care providers help review families’ applications. Corporate partnerships also extend to diapers, lactation support and education for growing families.

Welteroth’s own search for care led her to a Black-owned birthing center in Los Angeles. In December 2023, she started a fundraiser to cover care for one family. It brought in enough for two.

The organization formally launched in April 2024, drawing support from individual donors, companies and a network of family funders. That network includes musician John Legend and Chrissy Teigen.

The race organizer lists birthFUND as its official philanthropic partner, with a dedicated fundraising page for supporters of the team.

Their return follows another Houston project. Earlier this month, Rowland and Knowles joined Beyoncé at the opening of the 31-unit Knowles-Rowland House, a permanent supportive housing development. Residents are scheduled to start moving in November 1.

For the walk, participants will travel along Emancipation Avenue, starting near Arbor Street and finishing at Rosalie Street by Emancipation Park. The organizer welcomes children under six with a registered adult, and allows strollers and wheelchairs in the community walk.

The park will host a finishers village with food, music, local businesses and a birthFUND family zone. Registration is open, with the organizer listing a $35 fee. The organizer’s schedule, which is subject to change, places the first race heats at 8 a.m. and the birthFUND community walk at 9:30 a.m. local time on November 28.

item.title: Katt Williams Challenges Hollywood’s Limits On Black Films As He Builds His Own Studio
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Katt Williams explained why he’s building his own studio as he challenged the limits Hollywood places on Black-led movies.
item.content:encoded:
Katt Williams said Black films face tight limits in Hollywood, and he wants his own studio to help change that.

In a new USA TODAY interview, the comic laid out the thinking behind Kemet Movie Works, his film venture in Alabama.

“Nobody needs a complainer, even if they’re correct,” Williams said. “So I can talk blue in the face about what I don’t like about Hollywood.”

He said those complaints should lead him to act once he has a chance to do so. He also said Black films face tighter bounds on the stories they can tell than other films do.

His memoir recounts two times he turned down deals worth millions on principle, USA TODAY reported. He said the business too often loses sight of the people who pay to watch.

The studio effort has a home at Fort McClellan in Anniston, Alabama. Kemet’s site lists film, TV and music work, along with live shows, as part of its plan. That would give creators space to shoot work as well as places to show it.

The venture has been taking shape for some time. Williams credited Tyler Perry’s studio as an example during a 2025 visit to “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.”

Kemet’s stated mission is to help a wider range of voices bring film, TV and music projects to life. The firm ties that goal to the region’s Black cultural history, including the Chitlin’ Circuit, a network of venues where Black acts could work during segregation.

Miles College said in May that its deal with Kemet Productions would give students access to AI and augmented-reality film work at the Fort McClellan site. Based in Fairfield, Alabama, Miles is a historically Black college.

He is taking on new work beyond the stage.

Netflix announced in September that he would launch an original podcast on the service later this year. His stand-up shows are already on the service, including “The Last Report.”

His book takes up the question of who controls his work. The publisher says the book explores how he paid for his own tours and kept control of his work. Gallery/13A will release “Nine Lives, No Wives, and 69 Concubines” on October 20.
